source.title: How Does Preconditioning Guide Feature Learning in Deep Neural Networks?

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no apparent truncation or garbling affects the extracted results.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests how preconditioning and optimizer choice affect generalization, using test error and accuracy. It does not test memorization capacity or the specific interventions in V1–V8; the results below concern related settings outside those versions.
record.gate_note: Results on synthetic noisy-label data, MNIST correlation shift, CIFAR-10 correlation shift, and forward transfer bear on generalization but do not test the specific behaviors named in V1–V8. Out-of-distribution results are kept separate from in-distribution generalization claims.
record.test_reason: The optimizer comparisons test V4 in a new setting: held-out image classification under constructed correlation shifts. V4 does not explicitly exclude OOD evaluation. However, these experiments do not establish the version's limited-tuning condition, and their conclusions must remain specific to the reported tuning and distributions.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate but compresses an important distinction: alignment with task-relevant spectral components improves current-task ID and OOD performance, whereas uniform spectral emphasis at p = −1 best preserves features for the tested forward-transfer tasks. The theoretical feature-selection result is restricted to a single-ReLU population model.
record.recipe_differences: Studies covariance-power and optimizer preconditioning, rather than random-label memorization, width, architecture, batch size, dropout, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization depends on alignment between preconditioner power and teacher or invariant-feature spectrum; OOD optimizer rankings reverse across the two correlation-shift settings. In noisy-label experiments, trends reverse between high- and low-variance teacher alignment. p = −2 with AdaHessian is numerically unstable in Case Low.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM performs well when top PCs are invariant and remains near chance when bottom noise is invariant.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer-induced spectral preferences affect robustness to correlation shifts.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic regression test-MSE rankings reverse with teacher alignment; covariance-power and AdaHessian sweeps reproduce this dependence, including at matched training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preconditioner alignment with informative spectral directions determines robustness to label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Source-task preconditioning with p = −1 produces the best subsequent-task performance when the first layer is frozen.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Uniform spectral emphasis during source training can preserve features useful for forward transfer.

record.problems: OOD table reports mean ± standard deviation but no sample count for these results in the supplied text. The noise robustness figure's numerical values are figure-only; the text reports qualitative trends. The theorem is limited to a single-ReLU population model with Gaussian inputs, fixed readout, and rotationally symmetric teacher.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports separate OOD results for MNIST and for covariance-power sweeps in Table 2, plus qualitative noisy-label test-MSE comparisons in Figure 1 and transfer results in Figure 3. These were left out to prioritize the explicit CIFAR-10 optimizer comparison in Table 3; no claim version directly covers these settings.

untested.parts: Paired natural-label and fixed random-label fitting and held-out accuracy.
Width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.

The restriction to learning-rate and decay-schedule tuning is not established for the recorded CIFAR-10 experiment. Ordinary unshifted test performance, matched training performance, broader-tuning comparisons, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and language benchmarks are not tested by these rows. MNIST ID validation accuracy is used for hyperparameter selection and is not an independent test result.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipe changes.
Dropout interventions and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and rankings against other measures.
Influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 3 values and distribution descriptions match the supplied text. The record's assertion that the prompt excludes OOD results is unsupported. These results qualify an extension of V4 to correlation shifts; they do not independently establish its limited-tuning premise. Other relevant experiments are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; no random-label control.
Width sweep past interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.

The version concerns held-out benchmark performance under adaptive optimizers; the optimizer comparisons here are on OOD correlation-shift tasks, which the prompt treats separately. It also does not test the version’s tuning, weight-decay, switching, or language-model qualifications.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurement and comparison to other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

source_check.notes: The rows' notes claiming that OOD accuracy bears on no version conflict with their V4 links and should be removed. Section 3.2.1 describes ID-validation grid search for MNIST; Appendix G.3 does not establish the CIFAR-10 tuning search space.

statements.correction: CIFAR-10, 3-layer CNN, Test Low Acc: bottom noise invariant; top PCs shuffled relative to labels; K-FAC accuracy 76.1 ± 15.7%; SGD 9.9 ± 0.1%; Adam 12.8 ± 2.1%; uncertainties are standard deviations; comparison significance and strict limited-tuning eligibility not established; scope evidence for constructed correlation shifts.
statements.problem: The CIFAR-10 numbers and near-chance description are correct. The challenges label overstates this study's bearing on V4: the constructed shifts establish condition-dependent rankings, while eligibility for the limited-tuning condition remains unverified.
